questions.q: What does "lead with what matters most" mean for dashboard layout?
options: Widgets should be sorted alphabetically by title
The most important number or chart should be visible above the fold, without scrolling
Every widget should be the same size
The dashboard should only ever contain one widget
questions.explain: If a viewer has to scroll to find the one number they opened the dashboard for, the layout has already failed. The most important content belongs at the top.

questions.q: Why does restraint (fewer, well-chosen widgets) usually beat a dashboard that tries to show everything?
options: Every added widget competes for attention, and View Report links already provide a path to more detail
Dashboards with fewer widgets load data from a different server
Salesforce enforces a hard limit of 3 widgets per dashboard
Restraint reduces the number of required source reports to zero
questions.explain: A dashboard trying to show everything shows nothing clearly. A handful of well-chosen widgets, with View Report links for deeper detail, communicates far better than a crowded grid.

questions.q: Why is chart-type and color consistency across widgets and dashboards recommended?
options: A viewer who has learned to read one dashboard's patterns can read the next one just as fast
It's the only way to enable dynamic dashboards
It's required by Salesforce's platform limits
It reduces the number of reports a report type can expose
questions.explain: Reused visual patterns — the same chart type for the same kind of question, consistent color meaning — let a viewer transfer what they've already learned to new dashboards instantly.

questions.q: What makes a widget title like "Open Pipe This FQ" better than "Report 3"?
options: It automatically changes the chart type
Salesforce requires widget titles to include a fiscal quarter
It describes what the number actually tells a viewer, rather than just referencing the underlying report
It's shorter in character count
questions.explain: A good widget title communicates meaning at a glance. Naming a widget after what it tells a viewer — rather than an arbitrary report label — makes the dashboard self-explanatory.

questions.q: A dashboard has twelve widgets, inconsistent chart types for similar data, and its most important number is the eighth thing a viewer sees. Which habit should be fixed first for the biggest impact?
options: Renaming the dashboard itself
Converting all reports to Joined format
Moving the most important number above the fold
Changing the dashboard's folder sharing
questions.explain: While both restraint and consistency matter, burying the single most important number eighth defeats the dashboard's core purpose — a viewer shouldn't have to hunt for the one thing they opened it to see.
